answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to complete a unique, non-parallelizable computational proof tied to its public key before it may transact. Like a river that only flows one way, the work cannot be copied onto a second identity. The cost is tuned so one honest agent pays little, while a thousand fake identities face a wall of expense. Verified work is recorded on a public terrace of attestations, so the horizon of trust grows only from identities that paid the price, and fakes starve before they can earn.
